CB3-MUST-3.codeVersusDataCapabilityAssessment: SUBSTANTIVELY ASSESSED AND SOUND. syntaxClass is NOT caller-selected: it is read from a closed published registry, the declared value must EQUAL the registered value, and the coupling to the body-language enum is enforced in BOTH directions (a `code` language must be in the clone-preimage enum; a `data-document` language must not). CB3-MUST-5.title: The required partial-ownership Coverage disclosure has no publishable typed cause
CB3-MUST-5.correctionObserved: Three NativeCause members are registered and paired in ONE table (CLONE_OWNERSHIP_DISCLOSURE): ownership-missing -> body-language-ownership-missing, owner-unenumerated -> body-language-owner-unenumerated, owner-ambiguous -> body-language-owner-ambiguous. All three deficiencies are input-closure-incomplete; all three causes are registered, distinct and non-null.
CB3-MUST-5.vocabularyAloneWouldNotHaveBeenEnough: The source itself records that adding the enum members was necessary and NOT sufficient, because a vocabulary nothing derives and nothing enforces leaves the disclosure optional -- which is exactly what the retained-Run counterexamples showed (an unrelated budget-exhausted with a null cause satisfied the old prerequisite). The pairing is now DERIVED by the owning producer from committed ownership and THIS scope's subjects, and is never read from the claim being judged.
CB3-MUST-5.derivationProbedExhaustively: 19 cases against ownership records I constructed myself: missing/partial/ambiguous each yield their own non-null registered cause; partial is checked BEFORE any row is read so incomplete discovery cannot act as an implicit edition selection; two selected owners that AGREE owe nothing; a dangling unit record and a crate absent from the edition map are ambiguous.
CB3-MUST-5.selectionVersusEnumeration: Verified as distinct, which was the subtle half of this finding. A path compiled by no selected target (not-compiled) owes NOTHING. Owners lying entirely OUTSIDE the selection who disagree with each other create NO false ambiguity. A selected owner plus a conflicting UNSELECTED one is unambiguous. And ambiguity on a path outside this scope's subjects does not taint the scope, while the same record IS ambiguous for its own subject.
CB3-MUST-5.runAdmissionEnforcement: close_run derives the expected disclosure and raises three SEPARATE refusals -- COVERAGE_DIALECT_PREREQUISITE (false complete), COVERAGE_DIALECT_PREREQUISITE_UNDISCLOSED (null deficiency) and COVERAGE_DIALECT_DEFICIENCY_MISMATCH -- because three different things can be wrong with one claim. The old check stopped after two. Healthy Rust clone Runs still close.
CB3-MUST-5.publicCauseProjection: Only registered NativeCause members are used; no unregistered code invented.

priorAdvisoryDispositions.standing: All four actual Bv3 advisories are accounted individually with their limits preserved. None is promoted to a blocker and none is silently erased.

ADV-1.title: A schema-valid strict SUBSET of the pin inventory validates against PinnedPurgeDisclosure
ADV-1.assessment: Correct as recorded. Completeness of the pin ledger is a HOST obligation observed under the exclusive purge lease; a closed schema cannot express 'this set is all of them'. The contract states this itself. This is a limitation of schema validation, not a design defect, and it remains a qualification obligation rather than a design alternative.

ADV-2.title: EnforcementValue admits ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER; TEST.CONFINEMENT_CLAIM_REFUSED is a host-side join
ADV-2.assessment: Correct by design, and the important half is the warning: schema validity must not be read as an enforcement claim. The confinement truth-table join against permission-truth-tables.v9 is a host act. Consistent with this review's standing that all native/compiler/OS/crypto/storage observations in the kit are synthetic assumptions, never measured enforcement.

ADV-3.title: file, package and vcs-change appear in no matrix capability row
ADV-3.assessment: The matrix now publishes an explicit `inventory` capability naming exactly (file, enumerated), (package, manifest-declared) and (vcs-change, vcs-reported), so the matrix does now say which component produces them. This advisory related directly to CB3-MUST-3 and moved with it: the matrix grew from 60 to 66 cells over 6 language modes and 11 capabilities.

ADV-4.title: The '723 bytes for twenty-one crates' illustration is not reproducible from the published grammar
ADV-4.assessment: The illustration survives verbatim at identity-and-evidence.md:799 and is still stated as a flat constant: 'A Rust workspace of twenty-one crates already produces 723 bytes of raw map, against a maximum of 255.' I measured it myself rather than adopting either number, and the advisory is stronger than recorded: the value is not merely name-dependent, it can fall UNDER the limit at the same crate count. With short crate names (c0..c20) a 21-crate edition map canonicalises to 222 bytes -- below the u8 maximum of 255. Medium names give 400 and long names 946. So a reader could take 21 crates to be a threshold, which it is not.
ADV-4.designConclusionUnaffected: The DESIGN conclusion is untouched and correct: a map-valued component is not representable under a u8 length for ordinary valid inputs, so the fixed-width raw-32 treatment is right. The blind reviewer said the same from a different measurement (391 bytes).
ADV-4.whyNotPromoted: It changes no admission decision and no public output; two conforming implementations would build identically. It is motivational prose explaining WHY a fixed width was chosen, not a normative rule. Consistent with the instruction not to promote advisories to blockers, it stays an advisory.
ADV-4.suggestedCorrection: Qualify the sentence as illustrative and name-dependent, or cite a naming alongside the byte count.
